title: OECD Co-operative Research Programme (CRP) Research Fellowship 2027
description: The OECD's Co-operative Research Programme: Sustainable Agricultural and Food Systems funds scientists to spend 6-26 weeks doing international research at a host institution in a different CRP participating country, on topics related to the sustainability of agriculture, food, fisheries, or forests. Funding covers a return economy-class travel grant, a EUR 600-650 weekly subsistence allowance, and a EUR 165 terminal allowance. Applicants must be residents of one of the Programme's ~30 participating countries and propose a stay at a host institution in a different participating country; the host country is the applicant's own choice in coordination with the receiving institution, not fixed by the Programme. This listing uses France, home to the OECD's Paris headquarters and one of the longstanding participating countries, as a representative destination -- the actual host country varies by applicant and is confirmed as part of the application. This is the call for the 2027 fellowship cycle; applications are open now, with a deadline of 10 September 2026, midnight Paris time.
visaNote: This is a short-term research placement, not employment; entry/visa requirements for the chosen host country depend on the applicant's nationality and are their own responsibility.

title: Global FinTech Hackcelerator 2026 (Singapore FinTech Festival)
description: The Monetary Authority of Singapore's Global FinTech Hackcelerator invites fintech firms and solution providers worldwide to submit proposals against set problem statements (for 2026: AI for credit and fraud risk modelling in digital banking, wealth management for digitally native customers, and helping SMEs manage business risk). Up to 20 finalist teams are selected to work with a corporate champion and receive mentoring, then attend an in-person programme in Singapore from 11-13 November 2026, pitching at the Hackcelerator Demo Day during the Singapore FinTech Festival on 18 November 2026. Each finalist team receives a SGD 20,000 stipend (approximately USD 14,800 at recent exchange rates) intended to cover the team's own travel and accommodation costs, and one winning team per problem statement receives a further SGD 80,000 (approximately USD 59,200) in prize money. Application deadline: 14 August 2026.
org: Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) / Singapore FinTech Festival
visaNote: This is short-term contest participation, not employment; Singapore entry requirements for finalist team members depend on nationality and are their own responsibility.
